notes: US name 'Razr (2024)'; EU/global name 'Razr 50' - one physical device. LOCALE: the US product page for this model (motorola.com/us/en/p/phones/razr/razr-gen-4/pmipmgu37m4) now 301s to the razr family page and its archived snapshots are JS shells with no spec data, so all numbers come from Motorola's OWN AU page (motorola.com/au/en, device field 'motorola razr 50'), with the dimensions independently confirmed byte-for-byte on motorola.com/ae/en. EU locale pages (gb/de/fr/it/es) carry only an abbreviated EU-energy-label spec set and do NOT publish dimensions or mass. MOTOROLA CMS DEFECT: on the AU/AE pages the real dimensions are printed under the headline 'Body', while the headline 'Dimensions' contains an unrelated slab phone's numbers ('158.43 x 71.99 x 7.58mm' with Eclipse Black/Nebula Green/Lunar Blue colourways, i.e. a moto edge). The 'Body' value was used because its text is self-labelling ('Open:'/'Closed:') and matches this form factor; the '158.43' figures are NOT recorded anywhere here. mass_g 188 is Motorola's own hedged 'About 188 g' - recorded as printed, precision not added. PAIRING: no Motorola page states 'Razr (2024) = Razr 50' in words; the support is the shared catalogue code stem (US pmipmgu37m4 / GB-AU pmipmgu37my) - NOT identical, unlike the 2023 pair - so treat the alias as indicative, not manufacturer-confirmed. Dimensions printed W x H x D. displays[0].aspect null (Motorola prints only the main display's 22:9 here). materials.frame null - the AU page states no frame material. materials values come from Motorola marketing copy on the same page, not a spec table. announced/released null: no reachable manufacturer press release. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: hinge.type = 'flip'; hinge.axis = 'short'.
